articles.title: Houthi-run health ministry says airstrikes it blames on Saudi Arabia kill 27 near Yemen capital
articles.description: Nov 7 (Reuters) - At least 27 people were killed and 36 wounded in what the Houthi-run Saba news agency said were Saudi airstrikes on a village near Yemen's capital Sanaa on Saturday, in one of the deadliest reported attacks since fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned group resumed in July.Reuters could not independently verify the account. Saudi Arabia's Center for International Communication did not immediately comment, saying it would look into Reuters' inquiries.

articles.title: Syria denies plans to send troops to Yemen as Saudi military ties deepen
articles.description: Nov 7 (Reuters) - Syria has no plans to send troops to Yemen, a Syrian diplomatic source told state news agency SANA, dismissing reportsof a possible deployment while adding that military cooperation with Saudi Arabia could eventually expand.Saudi Arabia has been locked in worsening hostilities with the Iran-allied Houthis since July, when the widerconflict in the Middle East reignited the Yemen war, and Riyadh has since sought both defensive and offensive support from a range of allies.

articles.title: Syria aids Saudi Arabia with military advice and training amid Houthi attacks, sources say
articles.description: By Timour Azhari and Feras DalateyRIYADH, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Syria is aiding Riyadh with military advice and training as Saudi Arabia comes under attack by Yemen's Houthis, and has sent a limited number of military personnel to the kingdom, two Syrian military sources and a senior US official said.Saudi Arabia has been locked in worsening hostilities with the Iran-allied Houthis since July, when the Yemen war was reignited by the wider conflict in the Middle East, leading Riyadh to seek both defensive and offensive support from a range of allies.

articles.title: Airstrikes on a market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 20, Houthis say
articles.description: A spokesperson for the Iran-backed Houthi rebels' health ministry says that at least 20 have been killed in airstrikes on a market in southwestern Yemen. It would be one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces. The Houthi official said that 15 other people were wounded in Friday's airstrikes which he blamed on the Saudi-led coalition. Local authorities in Taiz acknowledged that an attack on a busy market killed and wounded people. But they blamed the Houthis. The Associated Press couldn’t immediately independently verify the claims of responsibility.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (November 6): Crude oil nears $100 again as fresh attacks dent peace talk hopes. What are experts saying?
articles.description: Crude oil price : Oil prices are making a comeback as fears of supply interruptions grow following recent tanker attacks. President Donald Trump has reiterated that Iran must obtain US consent for its nuclear activities. Concerns about potential supply challenges loom large, prompting Goldman Sachs to revise its Brent and WTI crude price projections upwards. Meanwhile, diplomatic negotiations involving Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar progress amid regional volatility.

articles.title: Yemen market bombing kills 20 as Qatar tries to avert new US-Iran clash
articles.description: AIR strikes killed at least 20 people at a market in south-west Yemen today as the Saudi-led coalition launched new bombing raids.Ansar Allah, as the Houthi movement which swept to power in Yemen in 2014 is formally known, said another 15 people were wounded in the bombing of al-Waziyah market in the province of Taiz.Taiz is a current battleground with the Houthis controlling most of the area and laying siege to the capital, which is still in the hands of the Yemeni government in exile based in Saudi Arabia.
